title: IES Cn4 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: IES Cn4 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: IES Cn4 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety. 92 to 96 days to harvest, 5.4 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: IES Cn4 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Cn 61. Ilagan Experimental Station. DA Reg. II bred it. It takes 92 to 96 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 5.36 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about IES Cn4 corn

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry
rows: Ilagan Experimental Station. DA Reg. II

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

IES Cn4 corn takes 92 to 96 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is 3.1 days faster than the average of the 19 glutinous open pollinated corn varieties with a day count, 97.1 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 5.36 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.09. It sits in the top quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.text: It was weak against corn borer, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant IES Cn4 corn

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 92 to 96 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.36 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of IES Cn4?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
